statement: Unresolved P0, P1 and P2 findings only. P3 hygiene is recorded in the capability rows of WHEEL_MASTER_CANONICALIZATION_REUSE_MATRIX_V1.json and is deliberately absent here so this register stays a decision list rather than a backlog.

severityPolicy.P0: Would invalidate current canonical governance. Must be resolved before the GATE15 execution lifecycle begins.
severityPolicy.P1: Will predictably block a future normal Gate. Must be resolved before the GATE15 execution lifecycle begins.
severityPolicy.P2: Canonical work exists but is not live-consumed, or causes avoidable token and rework cost. Repaired in-mission when deterministic and low risk; otherwise one bounded follow-up cohort.
severityPolicy.P3: Stale, duplicate or documentation hygiene only. Recorded, never allowed to derail Gate execution.

findings.title: No canonical regression baseline existed, so 70 pre-existing governance-suite failures were invisible and unattributable
findings.detail: At baseline HEAD the governance suite runs 1095 tests with 70 failures. None had been recorded anywhere. The GATE14 independent reinspection reported newUnrelatedFailureIdentities = 0 on the basis of 'targeted independent V2 and Gate14 validation' — that basis is accurate for what it measured, but it never ran the full suite, so this state was never surfaced. A GATE15 agent running the suite would have found 70 failures with no way to separate them from its own regressions.
findings.impactIfUnresolved: Every Gate from GATE15 onward either wastes a mission investigating pre-existing failures, or hides a genuine regression inside the noise.
findings.resolution: governance/master-matrix/REGRESSION_IDENTITY_BASELINE_V1.json records all 70 failure identities with a root-cause class, plus the 15 load-bearing checks that were recomputed PASS to justify classifying them unrelated. governance/tools/gate-preexecution-reuse-check.mjs consumes it as REGRESSION_BASELINE_KNOWN and mandates identity comparison rather than count comparison.
evidence: node --test governance/tests/*.test.mjs governance/gee-v1/tests/*.test.mjs governance/gates/GATE13/tests/*.test.mjs -> 1095 tests, 1022 pass, 70 fail, 3 skipped
governance-preflight.mjs GOVERNANCE_VERDICT PASS with blockingFindingCount 0 at the same HEAD
findings.requiredAction: NONE — resolved. Future Gates diff against the baseline.

findings.title: The GEE R2-R7 real-repository demonstrations are pinned to GATE13, whose historical seal no longer satisfies the hardened REQ-SEA-03 rule
findings.detail: governance/gates/GATE13/state/revisions/R0002/STATE_SEAL.json binds governance/gates/GATE13/contracts/EXECUTION_CONTRACT_R0001.json where REQ-SEA-03 (introduced later by the H3 seal-hardening program) requires the gate-local CURRENT_CONTRACT projection. GATE13 therefore resolves authorityState.sealValid = false, compileContext(GATE13) throws CONFLICTING_AUTHORITY:SEAL_INVALID, and every GEE demonstration pinned to GATE13 cascades: 19 of the 70 baseline failure identities across R2, R4, R5, R6 and R7.
findings.impactIfUnresolved: GEE R7 cannot produce a green real-repository benchmark, and any future reader will mistake a fixture-pinning problem for a broken engine. GATE13 itself remains COMPLETE_CONFIRMED and its closure is not in question.
findings.whyNotRepairedHere: Two candidate repairs exist and choosing between them is a strategic decision, not a wiring fix: (a) re-point the GEE fixtures at a work unit that verifies today, which changes frozen R7 evidence; or (b) issue a historical interpretation record for the GATE13 seal, which touches closed historical ground. This program is authorized for neither.
findings.requiredAction: One bounded follow-up cohort. Decide (a) or (b). Until then the 19 identities stay classified PREEXISTING_UNRELATED in the baseline and must not be counted against any Gate.
evidence: inspect-work-unit.mjs --work-unit GATE13 -> authorityState.sealValid false, reason SEAL_INVALID
gee-r7-eval-suite.test.mjs fails through gee-r7-recovery-child.mjs with CONFLICTING_AUTHORITY:SEAL_INVALID
The same chain executes cleanly against GATE14: R2 18.112x, R3 snapshot, R4 graph, R5 plan, R6 session all succeed
findings.fastPathImpact: NONE. The fast path compiles its own fixtures from the Gate being planned and never reads the GATE13-pinned R7 fixtures. Only the heavy R7 benchmark still depends on them.

findings.title: GEE R2-R6 had no consumer outside tests, so six closed revisions of work-reduction machinery were unreachable from any lifecycle path
findings.detail: Static import analysis of all 148 governance modules showed delta-engine.mjs, evidence-graph.mjs, router-engine.mjs, repair-containment.mjs, recovery-engine.mjs, repo-index.mjs, usage-ledger.mjs and content-addressed-store.mjs reachable only from test files. R2 had a CLI (context-compile.mjs) but nothing in the Gate lifecycle called it. The engines were not broken — they were unreferenced.
findings.impactIfUnresolved: Every future Gate pays full context and evidence cost while a closed, tested, fail-closed reduction stack sits unused. This is precisely the 'work already done but not linked' failure this program exists to end.
findings.resolution: governance/tools/gate-preexecution-reuse-check.mjs now executes R2, R3, R4 and R5 against a dynamically resolved reference work unit on every run, and reports the measured result. R6 was additionally proven end-to-end against GATE14 during this program and is documented in GEE_LIVE_USAGE_MATRIX_V1.json. No competing context system was created.
evidence: gate-preexecution-reuse-check.mjs --gate GATE15: GEE_CONTEXT_LIVE PASS (161288B -> 6544B, 18.112x), GEE_DELTA_LIVE PASS, GEE_EVIDENCE_REUSE_LIVE PASS, GEE_MIN_FRONTIER_LIVE PASS
R6 createWheelRecoverySession against GATE14 returned a full session and a recovery delta
findings.requiredAction: NONE — resolved. Gates should also call governance/gee-v1/tools/context-compile.mjs --work-unit <GATE> instead of loading canonical files wholesale.

findings.title: The ACTIVE_GATE succession primitive is implemented and hostile-tested but has never been called
findings.detail: governance/gee-v1/core/active-gate-succession.mjs implements evaluateActiveGateSuccession with exact pre-head, previous pointer, ledger prefix, activation digest and single-use authority binding. Its only importer is its test file, because no ACTIVE_GATE succession has been performed yet — the pointer still lawfully names GATE13.
findings.impactIfUnresolved: The first Gate that needs to move lifecycle ownership may edit governance/active/ACTIVE_GATE.json directly and bypass a fail-closed primitive that already exists.
findings.requiredAction: When a Gate moves the pointer, build an ACTIVE_GATE_SUCCESSION_RECORD and evaluate it through evaluateActiveGateSuccession under a single-use local authority. Do not hand-edit the pointer.
findings.fastPathImpact: NONE. The control plane plans only; ACTIVE_GATE succession stays lifecycle-owner semantics and is never triggered by START. Confirmed by FP19.

findings.title: A sealed execution contract pins live registry bytes, and unlike the ledger it has no migration containment
findings.detail: Every execution contract pins strategicRegistryReference.registrySha256. The registry has been lawfully amended twice: 706397af -> f5963314 -> aaa9efcd (the last by commit 3eb0641d, which canonicalized the GATE15-GATE40 mandates). Each amendment retroactively invalidates the registry pin of every previously sealed contract. For CLOSED gates this is already contained by design — validate-active-gate.mjs lines 22-27 deliberately stop re-authorizing a closed gate against a mutable registry. Ledger events have their own containment via REGISTRY_AUTHORITY_MIGRATIONS.ndjson. Sealed contracts of a gate that is still IN_PROGRESS have neither.
findings.impactIfUnresolved: Amending the registry while a Gate is IN_PROGRESS would invalidate that Gate's sealed contract, and validate-active-gate.mjs would return ACTIVE_GATE_NOT_AUTHORIZED / GATE_CONTRACT_INVALID until it was repaired.
findings.requiredAction: Operational rule, no code change: amend the registry BETWEEN Gates, never during one. If a mid-Gate amendment ever becomes necessary, it requires a contract succession in the same cohort. Sequential GATE15-GATE40 execution never triggers this.
evidence: validate-gate-contract.mjs on GATE14 R0002 -> REGISTRY_HASH_MISMATCH, pinned f5963314, live aaa9efcd
findings.fastPathImpact: NONE for a not-yet-started Gate. Operational rule stands: strategic registry amendments occur between Gates unless an explicit governed succession mechanism is used.

findings.title: Validator CLI flags are inconsistent, so a correct invocation silently validated the wrong gate
findings.detail: validate-state-revision.mjs takes --gate-id, validate-gate-authorization-authority.mjs takes --gate, validate-gate-contract.mjs takes --contract and --pointer with GATE13 defaults, and the GEE tools take --work-unit. An unrecognised flag is ignored rather than rejected: `validate-state-revision.mjs --gate GATE14` silently reported on GATE13 and looked like a GATE14 failure.
findings.impactIfUnresolved: A future Gate can conclude its own artifacts are broken while actually reading GATE13's, and burn a mission on a phantom defect.
findings.resolution: The exact invocation for each phase is now recorded in WHEEL_MASTER_CANONICALIZATION_REUSE_MATRIX_V1.json#/minimumEvidenceFrontier and in the GATE15_40 capability matrix primitiveEvidence block, with the correct flag spelled out per validator.
findings.requiredAction: NONE — resolved by documentation. Harmonising the flags themselves would change 21 tool signatures and is out of scope for a linkage repair.
evidence: validate-state-revision.mjs --gate-id GATE14 reports valid true, resolvedBy NATIVE_EVENT_PIN

findings.title: R2 could not compile a context for any future Gate, so no future Gate could enter the GEE chain at all
findings.detail: context-wheel-adapter.mjs treated authorityState.consistent === false as an authority conflict and refused to compile. For a NOT_STARTED Gate that flag only means "this Gate’s status cannot yet satisfy someone else’s prerequisite" — the normal pre-execution shape, since a Gate carrying only its genesis import has UNANCHORED_LEGACY ledger trust. Every GATE15-GATE40 context compile therefore failed with CONFLICTING_AUTHORITY:TRUST_LEVEL_BELOW_REQUIRED, which is why the GEE liveness probes had to run against a closed Gate instead of the Gate being planned.
findings.resolution: The adapter now distinguishes the pre-execution shape from a genuine conflict, by an exact fingerprint: reason is exactly TRUST_LEVEL_BELOW_REQUIRED:UNANCHORED_LEGACY<ANCHORED_APPEND_ONLY, statusKnowledge ABSENT, sealValid false, canonical revision structurally valid, ledger status NOT_STARTED. Any invalid seal, seal/ledger disagreement, unverified ledger or structural violation still conflicts. The fact is not swallowed: it is carried into the bundle as a provenance-bearing PRE_EXECUTION_TRUST_LEVEL blocker.
proofReferences: governance/tests/gate-fast-path-control-plane.test.mjs (FP21 compiles a real GATE15 chain with every binding proven)

findings.title: GEE R2-R6 executed but the Gate lifecycle did not run through them
findings.detail: MGR-003 gave the layers a consumer, but that consumer was a liveness probe: it ran each engine against a closed reference Gate and, for R4, with r3Delta null. "The engine starts" was being read as "the lifecycle consumes it". No Gate plan was produced by R2→R3→R4→R5, so none of the reuse the stack computes could reach a Gate.
findings.resolution: gate-fast-path-control-plane.mjs compiles the chain for the Gate being planned and binds each arrow: every downstream layer records the upstream identity it consumed, and the control plane recomputes that identity independently and compares. A disagreement on any edge blocks. The admission checker now states explicitly that it probes rather than consumes, and checks that the lifecycle consumer exists.
proofReferences: governance/tests/gate-fast-path-control-plane.test.mjs (FP01-FP05 break each arrow; FP21 proves all five bind)

boundedDecisionList.question: How should the GEE R2-R7 real-repository fixtures, currently pinned to GATE13, be re-grounded now that GATE13's historical seal no longer satisfies REQ-SEA-03?
options: (a) Re-point the GEE fixtures and the frozen R7 benchmark at a work unit that verifies today (GATE14). Touches frozen R7 evidence.

(b) Issue a historical interpretation record for the GATE13 R0002 seal, in the same shape as LEGACY_STATE_BINDINGS, granting no permission and only declaring how the pre-hardening seal is to be read. Touches closed historical ground.
(c) Accept the 19 identities as permanently PREEXISTING_UNRELATED and leave the R7 real-repository benchmark red.
boundedDecisionList.recommendation: (b). It is the smaller change, it matches an established precedent in this repository, it grants no permission, and it leaves the R7 evidence frozen as it was closed.
boundedDecisionList.consequenceOfDeferring: None for GATE15-GATE40 execution. The 19 identities remain classified in the regression baseline and are excluded from any Gate's regression comparison.
